title: Cities and public health

draft.title: Cities and public health
card: During the Industrial Revolution, people moved from the countryside to towns to work in factories. Cities such as Manchester and Leeds grew very fast.
Many workers lived in crowded, cheap housing built quickly near the factories. Often several families shared a small space with no proper drains or clean water.
Waste often ran into the same rivers and wells that people drank from. Dirty water spread diseases such as cholera, which causes severe diarrhoea and can kill.
Disease fell once cities built sewers to carry waste away and supplied clean water. These changes took many years and came after outbreaks of disease.
draft.remember: Fast growth without sewers or clean water let disease spread. Better water and sewers cut it.

a.q: Why did cholera spread so easily in many industrial cities?
opts: Waste got into the water people drank
Factory smoke carried the disease through the air
Workers brought the disease from farms to cities
Cities had too few doctors to treat the sick
a.why: Waste often ran into rivers and wells used for drinking, so the disease passed from person to person through water. Poor medical care did not cause the spread, and the card does not link cholera to smoke or farms.
a.clue: Think about where people got their drinking water.

b.q: A town in northern England doubles in size in 30 years as mills open. Many people drink from a river that also carries away waste. What would most reduce cholera there?
opts: Building sewers and a clean water supply
Moving more families into houses near the mills
Opening more mills so workers can earn more
Asking people to leave the town for the countryside
b.why: Cholera spread through dirty water, so sewers and clean water cut off the cause. Higher wages might help people a little, but they do not stop waste from reaching the drinking water.
b.clue: Fix the way the disease spreads, not just the size of the town.

a.best: Waste got into the water people drank

b.best: Building sewers and a clean water supply
